overview: This Senate resolution marks one year since a shooting at Fort Stewart, an Army base in Georgia, on August 6, 2025, when a soldier shot and wounded five fellow soldiers, all of whom survived. It honors the victims and praises the unarmed soldiers who rushed to stop the shooter and give first aid, as well as the first responders. It also recognizes the religious leaders, mental health providers and others who have supported the base community since, and expresses support for the victims and their families. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it on August 6, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution rightly honors the victims and the soldiers who risked their lives to stop the attack and save others.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and does not address how to prevent similar attacks on military bases.
